zh.title: 土耳其航空敲定100架波音737 MAX 8訂單 另含50架選擇權
zh.summary: 土耳其航空最終確認購買100架737 MAX 8、可增訂50架，交付期2033-2037年
body: 土耳其航空與波音於2026年9月23日在紐約完成簽約，確認購買100架波音737 MAX 8客機，並取得另外50架同系列機型的選擇權。協議允許航空公司將部分訂單轉為尚未取得型別認證的737 MAX 10機型，以因應未來載客量需求變化。
波音官方新聞稿指出，這是土耳其航空迄今向波音下單的最大單通道機隊訂單，簽約儀式在土耳其總統雷傑普·塔伊普·艾爾多安見證下進行，正值第79屆聯合國大會期間。土耳其航空董事長穆拉特·謝克爾表示，新飛機將為從伊斯坦堡樞紐飛往國內外航線帶來更高效率與彈性。
交付時程排定於2033年至2037年間。波音商用飛機總裁兼執行長史蒂芬尼·波普形容此單延續雙方長期合作夥伴關係，並將支持土耳其航空業生態系發展。波音另稱737 MAX系列較取代機型降低20%燃油消耗與排放。
這項協議完成始於2025年的談判，當時土耳其航空宣佈計畫採購最多150架MAX客機，但附帶條件須與發動機供應商CFM International達成維護條款共識。路透社早先報導，雙方曾因LEAP-1B發動機長期維護安排價格僵持，土耳其航空一度考慮轉向空中巴士。
同期另一項2025年9月宣佈的協議顯示，土耳其航空已訂購50架波音787夢想客機（含35架787-9與15架787-10），另含25架選擇權。787-10將為該航司引進新機型，部署於伊斯坦堡往返美國、非洲、東南亞與中東的繁忙航線。土耳其航空與子公司AJet目前運營超過200架波音飛機。

en.title: Turkish Airlines Finalizes Order for 100 Boeing 737 MAX 8 Jets with Options for 50 More
en.summary: Turkish Airlines confirms 100 737 MAX 8 firm order; 50 options; deliveries 2033-2037
body: Turkish Airlines and Boeing finalized an agreement on 23 September 2026 in New York for a firm order of 100 Boeing 737 MAX 8 aircraft plus options for 50 additional 737 MAX jets. The deal includes substitution rights allowing the carrier to switch to the larger, not-yet-certified 737 MAX 10 as demand develops.

Boeing's press release describes the agreement as Turkish Airlines' largest single-aisle order from the manufacturer. The signing took place in the presence of Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan during the United Nations General Assembly. Turkish Airlines Chairman Prof Murat Şeker said the new MAX aircraft will bring greater efficiency and flexibility to operations from the airline's Istanbul hub.

Deliveries are scheduled from 2033 through 2037. Boeing Commercial Airplanes President and CEO Stephanie Pope called the order a reflection of the trust and shared vision defining the long-standing partnership. Boeing states the 737 MAX family reduces fuel use and emissions by 20% compared with the airplanes they replace.

The agreement concludes negotiations initiated in 2025, when Turkish Airlines announced plans for up to 150 MAX jets alongside a separate 787 Dreamliner order. Talks had stalled over maintenance terms with CFM International, the GE Aerospace-Safran joint venture that produces the LEAP-1B engines powering the 737 MAX. Reuters reported the carrier had considered abandoning the Boeing purchase in favour of Airbus if engine negotiations failed.

The MAX purchase builds on Turkish Airlines' 2025 commitment for up to 75 787 Dreamliners (50 firm, 25 options), including 35 787-9s and 15 787-10s plus 25 options. The 787-10 will be a new variant for the airline, slated for high-density routes between Istanbul and destinations in the United States, Africa, Southeast Asia and the Middle East. Turkish Airlines and its subsidiary AJet currently operate more than 200 Boeing aircraft.
